title: Build par-release

proofs.pass: (?s)(?=.*PASS  release mode and accepted)(?=.*PASS  release mode and rejected -> exit 3)(?=.*PASS  default mode -> the assessment is never called)(?=.*, 0 failed, 0 not judged)

proofs.run: OUTSIDE (a Developer ID notarised build and the install into /Applications): sh scripts/install.sh <notarised build> then spctl -a -vv /Applications/Whoosh.app

owner: Only the owner can end three parts. (1) The notarised build: the Apple Developer ID account and the notarytool credentials; then `WHOOSH_INSTALL_RELEASE=1 sh scripts/install.sh <label>` must print 'gatekeeper: accepted' (proof 1, lead). (2) The Mac licensing provider (Polar or another checkout), after which a test-key unlock can be built. (3) The update feed: an updater that reads a feed on the network conflicts with 'nothing leaves this Mac except the relay'; the owner says where the feed lives (or that updates are delivered another way) before any Sparkle code is added. Also open: crash reports pick.
notes: Built in this pass: the release mode of scripts/install.sh (WHOOSH_INSTALL_RELEASE=1, exit 3, install.sh lines 151-167) with its self-test cases (release accepted, release rejected, default never calls the assessment) and one broken copy; docs/RELEASE.md section 'Release mode of install.sh'. Proof 1 cannot be run without the owner's credentials: it is the exact acceptance line, kept so the runner shows it as outside. Not built, no code exists: Sparkle updater and appcast fixture, licence unlock (needs the owner's picks above). checks/licence-check.py is a dependency licence scan and is not a proof here. Earlier evidence: the r83 install proved the stamp read back on an ad hoc build in ~/Applications only (_captures/tests/r83/summary.txt line 5).
